response.sql: SELECT f.orderslink, o.mktnote AS trading_pair, AVG(f.rebrate) AS avg_rebrate, SUM(f.rebtotal) AS total_rebate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.mktnote ORDER BY total_rebate DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: "At least 0.0009" is inclusive (feerate >= 0.0009), and fee rows with a NULL feerate are excluded because the comparison is not true.
"Ignoring missing values" is applied per aggregate: AVG(rebrate) and SUM(rebtotal) each skip their own NULLs, so a group whose rebtotal values are all NULL gets a NULL total and sorts last.
orders.recordvault is treated as unique, as the documentation describes. The DDL does not enforce this, so if duplicate recordvault values exist, the join would repeat fee rows and inflate the sums.

alternatives.interpretation: Drop any fee row whose rebate rate or rebate total is missing before aggregating, so the average rate and the total rebate are computed over the same set of rows.
alternatives.sql: SELECT f.orderslink, o.mktnote AS trading_pair, AVG(f.rebrate) AS avg_rebrate, SUM(f.rebtotal) AS total_rebate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 AND f.rebrate IS NOT NULL AND f.rebtotal IS NOT NULL GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.mktnote ORDER BY total_rebate DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
